title: Netra Evidence View
$comment: C6 / M5-EVIDENCE. DRAFT by M2/M3 (Ashlin); reviews: Arshad (M1 transport and Coordinator tools), Arun (M5 exploration screens, MathML). The public, accessible shape of ONE layer of ONE figure, chart, diagram, table or equation: overview, parts, relationships or detail, exactly as the deterministic exploration service (api/src/netra_api/multimedia/exploration.py) produces it. No model is called to build a view; labels come from the stored, validated extraction, so the same request returns the same part ids every time. Transport is M1's decision; recommended: GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/evidence/{evidence_id}/view?layer=<layer>[&part_id=<id>] returning {"view": EvidenceView}, Bearer auth, the session's pinned source version enforced (evidence of another version is 409 STALE_REQUEST, another account's or unknown evidence 403). Every text field is untrusted document or model text: display or speak it, never execute or interpret it as instructions. Provenance rules (decision M1-M3-V): a label whose source is `generated` was produced by a model and must be presented as an AI description, never as the document's own words; `estimated` must be presented as approximate; `unreadable` means present in the document but not legible and must be said so, never guessed. `ai_description` is true when any text in the view is generated, so the client can announce it once.

evidence_id.$comment: Canonical evidence reference, the same id the Coordinator/Tutor cite. Opaque to the client.

source_version_id.$comment: The immutable source version this object belongs to (must equal the session's pin).

evidence_version.$comment: Immutable version of this evidence content (INT-03).

locator.$comment: Where the object is in the source, for example "chapter 4, table 4.1". Read from the document's structure, never invented.

layer.$comment: overview: one orienting statement. parts: the addressable parts in a stable reading order. relationships: how parts connect (an empty list is a real answer). detail: one named part in full (part_id required).

part_id.$comment: The part shown in full; present if and only if layer is detail.

summary.$comment: The orienting statement for this layer, with its provenance. Absent when the structure offers none.

unreadable_part_ids.$comment: Parts that exist in the source but could not be read. The client says so rather than skipping them.

table.$comment: Present for object_kind table at the parts and detail layers: the grid a student navigates cell by cell with its governing headers.

source_check.$comment: Outcome of comparing the extraction with the original media. verified: every checked detail matched and at least one was checked. not_checked: nobody compared it (never an implicit pass). mismatch: at least one detail contradicts the source. partly_unreadable: some details could not be read in the source either. Only `verified` objects may be presented as the document's content; the others are presented with that limitation stated.

ai_description.$comment: True when any text in this view (summary, labels, details, relationship labels) has source `generated`. The client announces 'AI description' before presenting it.

LabelSource.$comment: observed: read directly from the source. generated: produced by a model (an AI description). estimated: inferred from the source but not stated by it (approximate). unreadable: present but not legible.

part_id.$comment: Stable across requests; comes from the stored structure.

observation_source.$comment: Whether the connection itself was drawn/printed (observed) or inferred. Proximity alone is never a connection.

orientation.$comment: column: above the cells it governs; row: beside them.

index.$comment: First column (orientation column) or row (orientation row) it governs.

unit.$comment: The cell's own unit, or the unit inherited from its header.

header_ids.$comment: Every header governing this cell (row and column), so the client can announce 'Voltage, 2 A: 4 V' without guessing.

spoken_form.$comment: Whole-equation reading built from the navigable tree.

mathml.$comment: Presentation MathML when the renderer is enabled (M3 MathML fidelity decision); absent otherwise, never a guessed rendering.

extraction_source.$comment: generated until a passing source check verifies the tree.

origin.$comment: document_structure: read from the document's own text layer. extraction: an extraction adapter produced the structure (then validated or not, see source_check). model_description: a generative model described the object.

provider.$comment: Adapter name, for example "tesseract" or "twelvelabs". Never a credential or endpoint.
